gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-north: Noto Sans Old North Arabian reads dense and upright, its tall lowercase band ending in terminals that flare outward like tongs. Edo SZ is the showpiece, a single-nib outline with cast-iron stature, while the body does the quiet, compact work of carrying text.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Chunky, open, unfussy. Noto Sans Old Turkic keeps its wide-mouthed curves clear beside Edo SZ, whose compass-pencil lines never waver in thickness.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-osage: Big, round, inflated shapes. Edo SZ matches that mood with rims as thick as its stems, and Noto Sans Osage fills each line with sweeping bowls that never close up.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Tall cast-iron lowercase meets compressed ascenders. Edo SZ draws every stroke free of thick and thin, while Noto Sans Palmyrene lets its curves stop short and keeps the text lines tidy and modern.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-psalter-p: Edo SZ traces its cast-iron lowercase with a single marker line, never swelling or thinning anywhere. Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi, with gaping e mouths, can sit at a modest size beneath.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Steel-cable outlines, glass-porthole counters. Edo SZ is happiest big and brief, its lines showing no thick-thin shift, while Noto Sans Rejang opens every c, e, s and a so running text stays legible.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Noto Sans Sharada reads bulky and generous, its open c forms never closing into rings. Edo SZ's wire-like letters sit above it, light against heavy.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-syloti-na: Clean and confident, Edo SZ draws its cast-iron lowercase like a thread of ink, never swelling or tapering. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri then carries paragraphs with short ascenders, tall x-height and an a that breathes.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Clean lines everywhere here: Edo SZ is best at monumental lowercase with no hairline-to-stem shift, whereas Noto Sans Tagalog does its work in a dominant middle zone with generous gaps in every curve.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Noto Sans Tai Tham reads like chalkboard lowercase crowding toward the capital line, each c plainly open. Edo SZ is the standout, its curves matching its stems exactly and its cast-iron stature unmistakable.
